title: Core RDK Entertainment Platform
description: RDKE is an open, modular foundation for entertainment platforms, built on reusable components, consistent APIs, and hardware abstraction. RDK8 advances app infrastructure through Firebolt Connect, supporting standardized, scalable delivery for web and native apps across RDK-powered devices.
release_overview: Released as a Development Preview, RDK8 enables early validation of key capabilities, accelerates ecosystem readiness, and reduces integration risk. It also provides a clear signal of platform direction, helping operators and partners plan product roadmaps and investments with greater confidence.

why.title: Why choose RDK-E?
why.description: RDK-E standardizes core platform functionality while allowing operators, OEMs, and technology partners to focus on creating differentiated user experiences and services. The platform provides a layered architecture that improves portability, maintainability, and time-to-market.
cards: Open and reusable
An open, modular platform built from reusable components that can be configured across STB entertainment platforms.
Consistent interfaces
Common APIs and services that help applications work consistently across diverse device platforms.
Hardware portability
Layered abstractions that reduce hardware coupling and simplify integration across SoCs and vendor platforms.
Faster delivery
Reusable platform capabilities that help operators, OEMs, and technology partners focus on differentiated experiences.

benefits.title: Key benefits of RDK8
cards: Early validation of next-generation app delivery

Gives developers and partners an opportunity to validate standardized app onboarding and integration through Firebolt Connect, including support for new App Managers and container-based technologies such as DAC 2.0, while reducing late-stage risk.
Accelerated app lifecycle readiness
Enables earlier validation of app lifecycle behavior through Firebolt Connect, helping ensure alignment with W3C standards, Firebolt 8.0, and more consistent app behavior across devices.
Faster ecosystem enablement and feedback
Allows developers, OEMs, and silicon partners to test on real implementations sooner, gather practical feedback, and reduce fragmentation by enabling vendors in parallel rather than sequentially.
Lower risk for operators
Helps operators assess new capabilities early without impacting live deployments, supporting more confident planning and adoption.
Faster app time to market at scale
Standardized app onboarding and validation through Firebolt Connect streamline optimization and support repeatable deployment across the RDK ecosystem.
Early performance and stability insights
Gives developers visibility into CPU, memory, GPU, and I/O performance on real hardware before field deployment.
Lower long-term platform costs and smoother user experience
Improved performance and power efficiency, driven in part by Vulkan adoption, help reduce long-term costs while enhancing the user experience.
Revamped OSS Model
Enables flexible, platform-specific OSS integration, improving adaptability and driving greater community reuse and contributions.

architecture.title: Everything in the Core RDK platform
layers: Firebolt apps, the Lightning reference UI and the Firebolt framework — where portable third-party and OTT streaming apps run.
A single, consistent implementation of core device functionality — the Thunder framework, entertainment services, media and DRM, and device management.
BSP, device drivers, HAL implementations, SoC adaptations and Linux OS integration — abstracting hardware differences behind the vendor layer.
cards: Core RDK components
The middleware-layer components that deliver a single, consistent implementation of core RDK-E device functionality.
Northbound APIs
Standardized APIs the middleware exposes upward to the application layer, giving apps consistent access to device capabilities via Thunder and Firebolt.
Southbound APIs
The Hardware Abstraction Layer (HAL) between middleware and the platform layer — standardized interfaces that abstract hardware differences.
Hardware specification
Reference hardware requirements and device specifications defined for the Entertainment OS platform.
